# Independent audit of midpoint determinant margins and endpoint credit

Audited `candidate 986ab1688d049a3b`
in full, including the supplementary threshold (3a). Result: PASS.
The exact verifier `supporting computation verify_simplex_midpoint_margins_and_endpoint_credit.py`
also runs successfully. No mathematical correction is required.

## Determinant and coordinate margin

After sorting the row maxima decreasingly, replacing the first row by
the row sum preserves the determinant up to the irrelevant preceding
row-permutation sign. Column stochasticity makes that row all ones.
Subtracting p_i/2 times it from each other row centers entries in
[-p_i/2,p_i/2]. Hadamard therefore gives the stated factor
N^(N/2)/2^(N-1). All row maxima are at most one. The number of remaining
factors bounded by p_j is exactly N-j+1=floor(N/2)+1, including N=3.
Its doubled value exceeds N, giving the strictly positive margin.
The separate N=2 calculation is correct.

The supplementary inequality uses row norm squared <=p_i r_i and
the AM--GM product bound prod r_i<=1, since the total row sum is N.
It consequently gives p_j>=4^(-(N-1)/(N-j+1)). Both estimates apply
to the SAME ordered row maximum, so their maximum can indeed be used.
The second threshold converges to 1/16; subtracting 1/N leaves the
stated positive limiting margin. No continuous determinant optimizer
or equality classification is required.

For every p in A, the barycentric matrix of (p+C)/2 is column stochastic
and has absolute determinant exactly its volume ratio 2^-d. Its row
maxima are (lambda_i(p)+h_i)/2. Its containment in B also bounds the
width of lambda_i on C by two. Both observations are valid even when
A and C themselves protrude outside B. The selected high-coordinate
indices may vary with p; the subsequent argument correctly retains
their indicator multiplicities instead of intersecting them.

## Actual one-direction endpoint costs

The cap convention is correct: lambda_i(x)+beta z>=b_i has thresholds
b_i+beta on A at z=-1 and b_i-beta on C at z=1.
Brunn--Minkowski yields a<=V from ((a^(1/d)+V^(1/d))/2)^d<=V.
For r=(a/V)^(1/d), homothety of all C toward a maximizing point of
lambda_i gives a contained cap subbody of volume a and threshold
h_i-W_i r. This lower bound uses actual d-volume, not a section law.

For every tilt, either its C cap already has mass >=a, or its C
threshold is STRICTLY larger than h_i-W_i r. The latter gives the
strictly smaller A threshold b_i+beta<T_i=2b_i-h_i+W_i r. In either
branch the actual sum captures at least A intersect {lambda_i>=T_i}.
Thus (8) holds before taking the infimum. Closed-cap endpoints are
safe because all bodies are full dimensional and the functionals are
nonconstant. The exact constant outer tilt regimes and continuity
between them also prove attainment of the infimum.

Under r+sigma<delta_N, each of the at least j pointwise high coordinates
has lambda_i(p)>T_i, using W_i<=2 and b_i<=1/N+sigma. Integration gives
sum e_i>=j a with no fixed subset of directions or diameter assumption.
The one-direction full-credit criterion in Section 5 follows from
the same homothetic cap argument after splitting according to whether
the A cap is full. Its upper bound e_i<=a comes from the negative
large-tilt regime, with the correct orientation.

## Scope and verifier

The three lifted fibers are realized exactly by their convex hull:
the only potentially new middle contribution is (A+C)/2, already
contained in B. Endpoint integer fibers remain unchanged. Hence the
costs are genuine ambient cap costs of that actual source.

The proof optimizes each integer tilt independently for specified
continuous facet directions. It neither chooses a center controlling
all directions nor substitutes midpoint-body normalized cap fractions
for endpoint costs. The final numerical distinction is valid: the
vertex-shifted half-simplex has sum 1+d(1-2/N)^d, and the verifier's
N=16 strict comparison is exact. The verifier checks determinant and
constant arithmetic; the geometric cap-credit proof is established
by the preceding independent argument, not inferred from its finite
matrix tests.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
